title: CCPA & California Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete CCPA compliance checklist for California residents and businesses. Protect your privacy rights and ensure legal compliance with step-by-step actions.
intro: This comprehensive checklist helps California residents exercise their privacy rights and assists businesses in achieving CCPA compliance. Follow these actionable steps to strengthen your privacy protection under California's consumer privacy laws.

items.task: Submit 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' requests to data brokers
items.why: Data brokers profit from selling your personal information to advertisers and other companies without your explicit consent.
items.howTo: Visit major data broker websites like Acxiom, LexisNexis, and Spokeo. Look for their CCPA opt-out forms or 'Do Not Sell' links, usually in the footer. Submit requests for all family members.

items.task: Request personal information disclosure from companies you interact with
items.why: You have the right to know what personal information companies collect, use, and share about you.
items.howTo: Contact companies via their privacy policy contact methods. Request disclosure of: what data they collect, sources of data, purposes for collection, and third parties they share with.

items.task: Enable privacy controls on social media platforms
items.why: Social platforms collect extensive personal data and may share it with advertisers under broad terms of service agreements.
items.howTo: Go to privacy settings on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and LinkedIn. Disable ad personalization, limit data sharing with partners, and restrict profile visibility to friends only.

items.task: Opt out of personalized advertising with major ad networks
items.why: Ad networks track your browsing behavior across websites to build detailed profiles for targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Visit the Digital Advertising Alliance opt-out page and Google's Ad Settings. Disable personalized ads and cross-site tracking. Use a privacy-focused browser to prevent tracking cookies.

items.task: Review and limit app permissions on mobile devices
items.why: Mobile apps often request excessive permissions and may share location and contact data with third parties.
items.howTo: Go to Settings > Privacy on iOS or Settings > Apps & Permissions on Android. Review each app's permissions and disable access to location, contacts, and photos unless essential.

items.task: Request deletion of personal information from unused services
items.why: Old accounts continue collecting and potentially sharing your data even when inactive, increasing your privacy risk.
items.howTo: Identify services you no longer use. Submit CCPA deletion requests through their privacy portals or contact forms. Keep records of your requests and follow up if needed.

items.task: Create and publish a comprehensive privacy policy
items.why: CCPA requires businesses to clearly disclose data collection practices and consumer rights to avoid penalties up to $7,500 per violation.
items.howTo: Include: categories of personal information collected, sources and purposes, third-party sharing practices, consumer rights, and contact information for privacy requests.

items.task: Implement 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link
items.why: Businesses must provide an easy way for consumers to opt out of personal information sales as required by CCPA Section 1798.135.
items.howTo: Add a prominent 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link to your website footer and main privacy page. Link to a simple opt-out form or process.

items.why: You must verify consumer identity before fulfilling access, deletion, or opt-out requests to prevent fraud and protect personal information.
items.howTo: Create verification methods using at least two data points you already have about the consumer. Document your verification process and train customer service staff.

items.task: Set up systems to respond to consumer rights requests within 45 days
items.why: CCPA mandates response timeframes and businesses face enforcement actions for failing to respond to valid consumer requests promptly.
items.howTo: Create intake procedures for requests, assign responsible staff, implement tracking systems, and establish workflows for access, deletion, and opt-out requests.

items.task: Update data sharing agreements with third-party vendors
items.why: You remain liable for how your vendors handle California consumer data and must ensure they comply with CCPA requirements.
items.howTo: Review contracts with service providers, advertisers, and data processors. Add CCPA compliance clauses, data handling restrictions, and breach notification requirements.

items.task: Train employees on CCPA requirements and data handling
items.why: Staff mistakes in handling consumer requests or personal information can result in violations and damage to your business reputation.
items.howTo: Conduct training sessions on CCPA rights, proper data handling, request verification procedures, and escalation processes. Document training completion.

items.task: Understand new sensitive personal information protections under CPRA
items.why: CPRA expands protections for biometric data, precise location, and other sensitive categories with stricter consent requirements.
items.howTo: Review your data collection for social security numbers, biometric identifiers, precise geolocation, and health data. Implement additional safeguards and explicit consent mechanisms.

items.task: Prepare for CPRA's expanded definition of 'sharing' personal information
items.why: CPRA treats cross-context behavioral advertising as 'sharing' requiring new disclosures and opt-out rights beyond traditional sales.
items.howTo: Audit your advertising practices, third-party analytics, and social media pixels. Update privacy notices to disclose 'sharing' and provide opt-out mechanisms.

items.task: Implement data minimization practices for CPRA compliance
items.why: CPRA requires businesses to limit data collection and retention to what's necessary for disclosed purposes, reducing legal risk.
items.howTo: Review data collection practices, eliminate unnecessary fields, set retention schedules, and implement automatic deletion for expired data. Document your minimization efforts.

items.why: CPRA requires businesses to honor universal opt-out mechanisms like Global Privacy Control signals from browsers and extensions.
items.howTo: Update your website to detect and respect opt-out preference signals. Consider recommending a privacy-focused browser to customers for enhanced privacy controls.

items.task: Conduct privacy impact assessments for high-risk processing
items.why: CPRA emphasizes risk-based approaches to privacy protection and businesses benefit from proactive risk identification.
items.howTo: Assess processing activities involving sensitive data, automated decision-making, or large-scale collection. Document potential risks and mitigation measures.

items.task: Prepare for California Privacy Protection Agency enforcement
items.why: The new dedicated privacy agency has expanded enforcement powers and will conduct audits and investigations starting in 2023.
items.howTo: Review compliance documentation, ensure staff training is current, and establish relationships with privacy attorneys. Monitor CPPA guidance and enforcement actions.

pro_tips: Keep detailed records of all privacy requests and your responses - documentation is crucial if the California Privacy Protection Agency investigates your business.
Use a privacy-focused browser's built-in privacy tools to automatically send Global Privacy Control signals and block tracking cookies when browsing California business websites.
Set calendar reminders to review and update your CCPA compliance quarterly, as regulations and enforcement guidance continue evolving.
Consider hiring a privacy attorney or consultant if your business processes large volumes of California consumer data or faces complex compliance scenarios.
Join industry privacy associations and subscribe to privacy law updates to stay current on CCPA/CPRA developments and best practices.
